answer.exemplar: By AM-GM, (a+b)/2 >= sqrt(36)=6, so a+b >= 12. Equality when a=b=6, attaining the minimum 12.

questions.explanation: AM-GM gives a+b >= 2√(ab)=12. Equality at a=b=6, so minimum is 12.

questions.topic: Least product under a fixed difference
questions.stem: A note fixes a-b=4 and a=6. Compute ab.
questions.explanation: b=6-4=2, ab=6*2=12. Multiplying a by difference gives 24, the wrong value.

questions.learningObjective: Spot an error in repeated term
questions.stem: A note minimizes a+1/a and claims min 1 by AM-GM. Identify error.

options.text: The solver should have subtracted terms
The solver should have added terms
The solver should have multiplied terms
The solver forgot factor two; minimum is 2

questions.explanation: AM-GM: a+1/a >= 2√(a*1/a)=2. Forgetting factor 2 gives 1, too low.

questions.stem: A note fixes a+b=10. Explain why the maximum product is 25.

answer.exemplar: By AM-GM, ab <= (10/2)^2=25, equality when a=b=5, so the maximum product is 25.

questions.explanation: AM-GM gives ab <= 25. Equality at a=b=5 attains the maximum.
